title: What LLMs Do in the Shadows: Reading Context Reliance from the Unembedding Dark Space
abstract: arXiv:2610.23182v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Detecting faithfulness hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) is crucial for their safe deployment in high-stakes domains. Recent approaches address this by contrasting contextual against parametric knowledge utilization, yet measuring context reliance typically demands noticeable overhead, such as materializing attention maps, running additional forward passes, or training auxiliary probes. In this work, we show that context reliance can be estimated by projecting hidden states onto the dark space - directions that compose weakly with the unembedding matrix. Beyond its recognized function as an initial-token attention sink, we show that this subspace actively mediates context processing, and that its share of hidden-state norm - termed the Dark Matter Ratio (DMR) - provides a direct score of context utilization. Pairing DMR with a parametric knowledge score yields DarkLens, a lightweight faithfulness detector operating strictly

translated_title: 大语言模型在暗影中做什么：从Unembedding暗空间读取上下文依赖性
translated_abstract: 检测大语言模型（LLM）中的忠实性幻觉对于其在高风险领域的安全部署至关重要。近期方法通过对比上下文知识与参数化知识的利用情况来解决这一问题，然而测量上下文依赖性通常需要显著的额外开销，例如具体化注意力图、运行额外的前向传播或训练辅助探针。在这项工作中，我们展示了上下文依赖性可以通过将隐藏状态投影到“暗空间”——即与unembedding矩阵弱组合的方向——来进行估计。除了其公认的作为初始token注意力汇聚点的功能外，我们证明该子空间还积极参与上下文处理，并且其在隐藏状态范数中的占比——被称为暗物质比率——提供了上下文利用程度的直接评分。将DMR与参数化知识评分相结合，我们提出了DarkLens，一个严格在……上运行的轻量级忠实性检测器（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出DarkLens方法，通过将隐藏状态投影到与unembedding矩阵弱组合的“暗空间”并计算暗物质比率（DMR），无需注意力图、额外前向传播或辅助探针等开销，即可直接量化大语言模型的上下文依赖性，实现轻量级忠实性幻觉检测。
